scope: Kebu Liguey (K066) acceptance case 1 only: worker access and profile. The other 7 acceptance cases (real work discovery, applications, employer/recruiter workflow, the SAFA connected journey, meaningful integration, EN/FR/Wolof coverage, and the full verification standard) are explicitly NOT attempted in this slice, per the addendum's own instruction to select and complete one real acceptance case at a time.

mappedBeforeAnyCode.method: Background Explore agent inventoried user_profiles, network_profiles, opportunity_profiles, Studio/Library portfolio-adjacent tables, and every existing jobs/employer/applicant grep hit before any schema or code was written.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.userProfiles: Identity-only (name, email, age, residence_country, diaspora_status, business_stage, sectors, avatar_url). No skills/languages/experience/portfolio fields — confirmed, not assumed. Left untouched.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.networkProfiles: K067-owned, a different RLS/ownership history already hardened Oct 15 (20261011005205_network_profile_ownership.sql's column-grant pattern reused here, see below). Adjacent (sector, stage, languages, looking_for) but a networking/business directory, not a skills/experience taxonomy for employment. Deliberately NOT extended — mixing concerns would re-open that just-fixed surface for no reason.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.opportunityProfiles: Confirmed schema-isolated from any applicant/employment concept (docs/OPPORTUNITY-OS-MASTER-SPEC.md's stated law, verified true in code, not just in docs): only intake/personalization fields (main_goal, goals, interest_paths, resource_needs, starting_budget_band). No overlap.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.portfolioEvidence: No existing 'worker portfolio' concept anywhere. library_nodes/library_shares (K058, already built and tested) is the closest reusable mechanism — owner-scoped documents/folders/links with sharing — reused by reference rather than inventing new file storage.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.jobsRecruitmentConfirmedAbsent: Grepped the whole repo case-insensitively for job_listing|job_posting|applicant|recruiter|employer|job_seeker|worker_profile|liguey before writing anything: zero hits outside docs/audit files and unrelated Opportunity OS sales content (app/for-organizations, app/for-schools, app/compare, app/api/apply-kit).
mappedBeforeAnyCode.oneRowPerUserConvention: Confirmed two real precedents: eager creation via the auth.users signup trigger (user_profiles), and lazy-ensure on first API touch (ensureAfriqueIdForUser, called from app/api/me/profile/route.ts on every read). worker_profiles uses the lazy-ensure pattern — created on the first GET /api/liguey/profile, mirroring that precedent rather than inventing a third convention.

schema.migration: supabase/migrations/20261016180000_liguey_worker_profiles.sql — public.worker_profiles (user_id primary key references auth.users, same 1:1 shape as opportunity_profiles) and public.worker_profile_evidence (a join table to library_nodes).
schema.selfReportedVsVerified: Every writable column is self-reported. verified_at/verified_by are reserved for a future, explicit verification capability and are not granted to `authenticated` at all — table-level column GRANTs, not just RLS, mirroring network_profiles.is_verified's defense-in-depth convention (20261011005205_network_profile_ownership.sql). Nothing in the product ever sets these columns today, so every profile is, correctly and verifiably (tested below), entirely self-reported — no credential, score, or eligibility check was invented.
schema.discoverabilityDefaultClosed: is_discoverable defaults to false — a worker profile is private until its owner explicitly opts in, not exposed by default to any future employer/recruiter workflow (K066 acceptance case 4, not attempted here).
schema.evidenceOwnershipCheck: worker_profile_evidence's INSERT policy requires private.library_node_owner_id(library_node_id) = auth.uid() — reusing an existing SECURITY DEFINER helper (K058) that queries library_nodes, a DIFFERENT table than the one its caller writes to here, so there is no self-reference recursion risk in reusing it (unlike the room_members/business_members cases fixed earlier this session, where the helper and the policy's own table were the same table).
schema.uncapturedDependencyNoted: public.set_updated_at() is used by this migration's triggers but, like businesses/business_members, has never been defined in the canonical supabase/migrations/ chain — only assumed to pre-exist, already relied on uncaptured by 20261016120000_library_sharing.sql. Unlike the businesses bootstrap, this is a trivial, standard, unambiguous trigger idiom with one obvious correct implementation (verified byte-for-byte against the archived definition), so this migration defines it via `create or replace` to be self-contained rather than silently depending on drift.

apiAndUi.routes: app/api/liguey/profile/route.ts (GET lazily ensures and returns the profile; PATCH updates only the fields sent, using the same no-default-on-the-shared-base zod pattern established in lib/work/items.ts to avoid repeating that session's earlier default-leak bug) and app/api/liguey/profile/evidence/route.ts (GET lists links with the linked item's title; POST links an owned Library item; DELETE unlinks).
apiAndUi.ui: app/liguey/page.tsx (honest landing page — states plainly that discovery/applications/employer workflow/SAFA are not built yet, does not fabricate job listings) and app/liguey/profile/page.tsx + app/components/liguey/liguey-profile-panel.tsx (the actual profile editor: headline/bio/skills/languages/location/country/remote/availability/discoverability, a repeatable formal-or-informal experience list, and portfolio-evidence linking against the signed-in user's own Library items). Added a 'Liguey' entry to the main app nav (app/components/kebu-nav-shell.tsx) so this is genuinely reachable in the running app, not a hidden/unlinked route. Verified by typecheck/lint/build and inspection against the tested API/RLS — not by a real browser run, the same honest limitation recorded for prior UI additions this session.
apiAndUi.i18n: English only in this slice. EN/FR/Wolof coverage is K066 acceptance case 7, explicitly not attempted here.

verifiedScenarios.realSqlPGliteTests: tests/liguey/worker-profile.local.test.ts — 9 cases against the actual migration SQL applied verbatim on top of the real library_sharing migration, gated on KEBU_LOCAL_PGLITE_ROOT, run explicitly: creating a profile with self-reported fields; informal/life experience is accepted, not rejected; no client write can ever set verified_at/verified_by (column grants reject it, not just RLS); a profile is private by default from another worker; updating a profile and is_discoverable defaulting closed; a worker cannot create another worker's profile; linking an owned Library item as evidence; rejecting linking a Library item the worker does not own; removing an evidence link and a stranger reading none of it.
verifiedScenarios.mockedRouteTests: tests/liguey/profile-route.test.ts (8 cases) and tests/liguey/profile-evidence-route.test.ts (8 cases) — first-ever coverage for these new routes: lazy creation on first GET, racing double-create handled by re-reading rather than failing, camelCase-to-snake_case field mapping, invalid-experience rejection, 404 on updating a nonexistent profile, cross-origin mutation rejection, evidence linking/ownership-rejection/conflict/removal.
